Examples of sexual harassment include but are not limited to:

sexual comments or jokes

unwanted advances or propositions

intrusive questions about a person’s private or sex life or a person discussing their own sex life

unwanted touching, hugging, massaging, or kissing

coercion for sexual favours

the impact of jokes and comments as witnessed by others

Victimisation

No one who works for NWS who makes a complaint under this policy should experience victimisation for having made the complaint, regardless of whether the complaint is upheld. Similarly, a person who has supported another in making a complaint, or themselves been impacted by witnessing any form of bullying and harassment, should experience any form of victimisation.

Victimisation is unlawful and examples include but are not limited to:

exclusion or isolation at work

unreasonable allocation of work

marking down a performance assessment

oppressive management or micromanagement

intentionally blocking progression or preventing training and development opportunities

Third Party Harassment

When the source of inappropriate behaviour in the workplace is a person who is not employed by NWS or the NDA, this is called “third party harassment”. This can still result in an unacceptable work environment and legal liabilities for NWS and the NDA. In the same way that harassment by anyone employed by NWS will not be tolerated, NWS will apply the same standards to anyone you come in to contact with at work from outside the organisation.

Employees and colleagues are encouraged to report third party harassment to their line manager or the contract/project manager responsible for the third party.

Investigations into Allegations of Bullying and Harassment

The purpose of any investigation is to establish a fair and balanced view of the facts relating to an allegation of bullying and harassment. Any investigation will be given priority and completed without unreasonable delay.

NWS reserve the right to appoint a suitably qualified and external investigator to ensure that investigations are impartial and objective and carried out with discretion, sensitivity, and respect, both for the employee and others who are involved, including any witnesses to the bullying and harassment.

It is the intention of NWS to share information gathered during an investigation with the employee to whom the bullying and harassment grievance applies, but in certain circumstances, NWS and/or NDA may wish to protect individuals or confidential business interests and therefore NWS and NDA reserve the right to withhold certain information. In such circumstances, the employee will be advised as to why the information is withheld.

In most cases, informal resolution will be encouraged before enacting a formal process, however where informal action fails to deliver the required outcome, or where behaviour warrants consideration of formal action, a formal disciplinary process will be implemented.

Roles and Responsibilities

It is imperative that everyone sets the tone for NWS and the wider NDA Group and acts as a role model by their own behaviour and ensuring a supportive working environment. To always treat others with dignity and respect and to support and promote a culture and environment that is respectful and free of any negative behaviours.

Both the line manager and the employee have a specific role in the application of the Bullying and Harassment Policy, supported by the HR Team. It is important that everyone fully understands their role and responsibilities to aid transparency, consistency, and effective communication.

Leaders and Managers

It is imperative that the senior leadership team and managers set the tone for NWS and the wider NDA Group.

Demonstrate the NWS Values and to be aware of their own behaviours on individuals in the workplace environment generally.

Read the policy and the NDA Code of Conduct and be aware of what constitutes bullying and harassment, and victimisation.

Be prepared to challenge and tackle incidents or reports of bullying and harassment in accordance with this policy and alert to resolving potential issues.

Be supportive of anyone bringing a claim of bullying and harassment or who is the subject of allegations, and to treat them with sensitivity and being aware of the impact on them.

Report incidents to HR and to also seek support and guidance from HR.

Complete any relevant training to meet management responsibility to uphold this policy.

Employees and Colleagues

All individuals should be committed to high standards in delivering work and dealing with colleagues, this will not only be about the tasks people do but the effect of their words, how they interact/engage with others and tackling bullying and harassment.

Read the policy and the NDA Code of Conduct and be aware of what constitutes bullying and harassment, and victimisation.

Report their concerns about any acceptable behaviour, whether direct or witnessed to their line manager in the first instance, or HR or Trade Union Representative.

Be aware of the support available if needed, from Trade Union Representatives, Employee Assistance Programme, or the HR Team.

Human Resources Team

The HR Team provide a supportive and guiding role for line managers and employees in the application of the Bullying and Harassment Policy and the procedures and processes that underpin the key principles/commitments.

To ensure that line managers and employee(s) are provided with legally compliant, meaningful advice, and guidance in relation to both informal and formal stages of bullying and harassment matters.

To facilitate discussions between the line manager and employee during the formal stages of bullying and harassment matters and to ensure fair and consistent application of the policy including challenging behaviours that do not meet the NWS Values during the formal stages of a bullying and harassment grievance process.
